not_modelled.what: Subtraction of up to 20,000 a person of disability income reported as wages for permanent and total disability; each spouse takes it or the age deduction, whichever benefits more.
Exemptions for dependents (930 each) and blindness (800 a person).
Military retirement income of a Congressional Medal of Honor recipient is subtracted in full.

Railroad Retirement benefits: taxable Tier 1 is subtracted with Social Security (Line 5), and Tier 2 and other Railroad Retirement benefits reported as a taxable pension or annuity are subtracted in full (code 22).
Retirement income whose contributions were taxed by another state (while deductible federally) is subtracted, up to the contributions taxed there.
Wage subtractions for military basic pay, Virginia National Guard pay, combat zone pay, and federal or state employees earning 15,000 or less.
Income from U.S. obligations (Treasury bills, notes, bonds, savings bonds and some agencies) is subtracted.
Interest and gains on Virginia state and municipal obligations are exempt; the projection treats all municipal interest as other-state (taxed).
Subtractions for unemployment compensation, lump-sum annuity death benefits paid to a beneficiary, and long-term gains on qualified-business investments made 2010 to 2020.

approximations.what: A married couple filing separately: Virginia tests the income-based age deduction on the joint AFAGI of both spouses; the projection uses the filer's own federal AGI.
approximations.size: Only married-separate returns; up to 690 a year per spouse.

approximations.what: AFAGI is taken as federal AGI less taxable Social Security; Virginia also adjusts it for conformity additions and subtractions and takes out taxable Tier 1 Railroad benefits.
approximations.size: Nil for most retirees; conformity adjustments are mainly business depreciation items.

approximations.what: The standard deduction is always applied; Virginia requires a filer who itemized federally to itemize on Virginia Schedule A.
approximations.size: Depends on the household's itemized deductions; usually larger than the standard deduction for a federal itemizer, so the projection usually overstates tax for them.

approximations.what: The Spouse Tax Adjustment (Form 760 Line 17), a reduction of up to 259 for a joint return where both spouses have income, is not applied.
approximations.size: Up to 259 a year for a married couple filing jointly with two incomes.

approximations.what: The filing threshold (tax is 0 when VAGI is under 11,950 single or separate, 23,900 joint) is not applied.
approximations.size: Only very low incomes; the schedule tax there is a few hundred dollars at most.

approximations.what: Interest on U.S. Treasury and other exempt U.S. obligations is taxed (the projection cannot tell it from other interest).
All municipal interest is treated as other-state (added and taxed); interest on Virginia state and local bonds is exempt.

The age-65 exemption is applied to anyone 65 or older in the tax year; Virginia's test is age 65 on or before January 1 of the following year, and it is barred with the Credit for Low-Income Individuals (not modelled).
approximations.size: Only a person whose 65th birthday is January 1 of the following year.

approximations.what: Later years: the standard deduction is scheduled by statute (Va. Code 58.1-322.03(1)(b)): 9,200 / 18,400 for 2027, 9,300 / 18,600 for 2028-2029, and 3,000 / 6,000 from 2030 (the 2025 booklet says the amounts revert to 3,000 / 6,000 after 2026). The projection holds 8,750 / 17,500 (not indexed).
approximations.size: 2027: 450 x 5.75% = 25.88 a year too much tax for a single filer; from 2030: 5,750 x 5.75% = 330.63 too little (661.25 joint).
